extracted.intended_audience: IMLS program staff, museum grantmakers, museum leaders, and evaluators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for assessing Museums for America (MFA) grant projects, including partnership formation, use of evaluation, audience reach and effects, implementation fidelity, technology/staffing issues, and organizational impacts. Drawn from IMLS evaluation of FY2004–FY2009 MFA projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership involvement (whether projects involve partners)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percent of projects involving partners (e.g., 70% of projects engaged with partners; 40% worked with one or two partners, 27% with three or four, and more than 30% involved five or more).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On the survey, partnerships were defined as any outside organization which expended cash or in-kind resources such as goods and services on the project. Use counts of partner organizations and proportion of projects with partners as a metric of collaborative reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of partner organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify categories of partner organizations involved in projects: community organizations, educational institutions, government organizations, and museums and libraries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey breakdowns list subtypes (e.g., arts and culture, local businesses, youth organizations, elementary schools, four‑year colleges, state/city/local government, libraries, history/science/art museums). Report partner composition by category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of partners per project
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure how many partner organizations a project engaged (e.g., one–two, three–four, five or more).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to distinguish projects with narrow collaborations from those with broad multi‑partner networks; Exhibit III‑18/III‑20 provide example distributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal vs. informal partnerships and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish formal partnerships (e.g., Memoranda of Understanding to define roles, responsibilities, and budgets) from informal collaborations or advisory relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether roles, responsibilities and budgets are documented (MOUs), and whether advisory committees or advisors are engaged (consulting or voluntary). Formal agreements are evidence of clear role allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partner roles and functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the functions partners perform: narrowly defined tasks vs. long‑term evolving relationships that help define a museum's niche or community value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualitative interview examples include content experts, educational advisors, corporate/public health partners, local art councils, ethnic organizations, vocational programs. Document partner contributions and longevity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variation of partnering by project type
rubrics_metrics.description: Report partnership prevalence by primary activity area (e.g., Programming, Exhibitions, Digitization/Collections, Technology, Organizational Development).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Nearly all Programming projects worked with partners; Digitization/Collections projects were less likely to entail partners and when they did usually had one or two partners. Use cross-tabulation to show partner patterns by activity area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence of museum size and grant size on partnering
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze how museum size (small, medium, large) and grant award size (small/medium/large) affect likelihood and types of partnerships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings showed smaller museums more likely to engage partners (75% small/medium vs. 64% large); grant size made only slight differences. Report statistically significant differences where present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of evaluation activities within projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether projects included research and evaluation activities (39% indicated they undertook such work under organizational development activities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track if projects explicitly allocated resources for evaluation (surveys, data collection) and whether evaluation influenced project development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of IMLS outcomes-based planning and logic models
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of IMLS outcomes-based planning materials, including the logic model, in shaping goals and guiding project development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviewees found logic models lengthy but valuable; assess whether a logic model was used, whether it guided evaluation design, and whether it improved efficiency in working with external evaluators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formative evaluation and pilot-testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of formative evaluation methods (e.g., pilot tests, teacher forums, focus groups) to understand audiences and refine programming before full implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: testing visitor engagement and comprehension, identifying behaviors likely to be adopted, and using teacher/advisor feedback on curriculum guides. Score presence and quality of formative activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation methods employed
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of evaluation/data collection methods used: surveys (including SurveyMonkey), visitor tallies, website hits/comments, interviews, observations, pre/post-tests, teacher forums, focus groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different methods serve different goals (satisfaction vs. learning gains). Note when projects used rigorous methods (e.g., pre/post-tests) versus basic tracking (visitor counts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of external evaluators and capacity building
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether projects engaged outside evaluators for evaluation design, data analysis, and staff training; external evaluators may expand evaluation practices and internal capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess quality of evaluator engagement, whether the museum used the external evaluator to train staff, and downstream expansion of evaluation tools across the institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation limitations and challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Barriers to effective evaluation including cost, lack of internal evaluation knowledge/capacity, and difficulty identifying meaningful short‑term indicators for long‑term goals (e.g., civic engagement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document specific constraints (budget, staff skills) and how museums mitigated them (hiring evaluators, using IMLS tools). Recognize that some ambitious outcomes may lack short‑term measurable indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project completion and unplanned activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether projects were completed as planned, and the frequency/types of unplanned activities (15% reported conducting unplanned activities such as upgrades, inventory, database development).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use completion rate as implementation fidelity metric; document timeline extensions and reasons; distinguish core deliverables vs. reasonable scope changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation timeline management
rubrics_metrics.description: How schedule changes or other museum activities (e.g., opening a major exhibit) affected project timelines and whether projects adapted constructively (e.g., incorporating construction into visitor experience).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess contingency planning and adaptive responses to scheduling conflicts; evaluate whether timeline extensions were managed and documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness and reliability of technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Suitability of selected technologies for visitor engagement and durability (e.g., touch-screens failing, microphone durability), and decisions about streaming vs. on-demand content due to bandwidth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate technology through pilot-testing, robustness, maintenance demands, visitor interaction patterns, and fallback solutions (e.g., taped content, live facilitators).

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing stability and volunteer management
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact of staffing changes and turnover on project records and implementation; strategies such as training volunteers, using log books to capture experiment details, or hiring to fill skill gaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess staffing risk, documentation practices, volunteer training systems, and whether the grant's prestige helped prioritize work during transitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing cultural/workflow differences with partners
rubrics_metrics.description: How differences in organizational size/culture between partners (e.g., small museum vs. large library bureaucracy) affect collaboration and what adaptations were made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document initial concerns (pace, bureaucracy) and eventual benefits (value of documentation, resource access); assess partnership management practices and conflict resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic scope and resource alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensuring project scope matches staff time, technical capacity, and translation needs (example: ambitious bilingual website translation proved infeasible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether objectives were realistic relative to resources; document scope reductions or substitutions (e.g., partial signage in another language) as mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with institutional mission and strategic goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects should be institutionally relevant and individually tailored to museums’ mission and strategic goals; grants often prompted institutional re-thinking of strategy/mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate fit between project objectives and museum mission, and whether projects produced institution-wide alignment or strategic changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility and interdisciplinarity as program strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: The MFA program's flexibility supports interdisciplinary, experimental, and institutionally relevant projects across content areas and engagement strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing programs, value cross-cutting activities and experimentation; document innovative approaches and their institutional relevance even if nonstandard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary activity area classification and resource allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorize projects by primary activity (Programming, Digitization/Collections, Exhibitions, Technology/Online Resources, Organizational Development) using resource allocation to identify focus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use primary-area classification to compare activity patterns; note that Programming, Digitization/Collections, and Exhibitions represented the greatest allocation of resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience groups served (breadth of audiences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure which audience groups a project served: general audiences, museum staff, targeted community members, professional audiences, policymakers; and subgroups such as students, youth, families, seniors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report percentages (e.g., 83% served general audiences, 68% museum staff, 54% targeted community members, 46% professional audiences) and number of distinct audience groups per project (range 1–16; mean ~7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Age groups served
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure age-based reach: adult and family groups vs. school-aged children; breakdowns (e.g., adults 26–64, multi-age families, K–5, grades 6–8, 9–12, preschool, seniors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report proportions (e.g., 92% served adult and family groups; 72% served school-age children) and average number of age groups per project (1–8, mean ~4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience effects — reached new audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the project reached new audiences such as youth, minorities, and families (73% reported reaching new audiences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use survey/self-report evidence to document new audience recruitment; disaggregate by project type where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience effects — increased commitment by existing audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence that existing audiences demonstrated increased commitment (64% of projects reported increased commitment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure indicators such as repeat visitation, deeper engagement, memberships, or sustained participation; compare by museum size and grant size where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience effects — increased audience access
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which projects increased audience access to museum resources (46% reported increased access through strategies like expanded hours and mobile programming).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document access strategies (expanded hours, mobile programming, online resources) and quantify increases in accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall audience effect occurrence
rubrics_metrics.description: Percent of projects reporting at least one positive audience effect (93% of responding museums that reached out to external audiences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use presence/absence of any positive audience effect as high-level outcome metric; further disaggregate by type of effect and project area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustaining new audiences (success of retention efforts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-reported characterization of sustaining new audiences: not at all successful / somewhat successful / very successful (99% at least somewhat or very successful; 49% very successful).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use follow-up measures and long-term tracking where possible to substantiate self-reports; report percentages and qualitative evidence of sustained engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post‑grant longer-term effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of impacts persisting three or more years post-completion (e.g., reaching new audiences, increasing visitation, receiving greater requests for materials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect longitudinal data or retrospective self-reports for grantees with projects completed 3+ years earlier; compare characteristics of projects/institutions with persistent effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational capacity effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect of grants on institutional capacity (98% reported at least one organizational effect), including increased knowledge, skills, staff capacity, fundraising ability, and reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure changes in staff skills/training, internal systems, fundraising outcomes, ability to leverage resources, and reputation; report both short‑ and longer‑term capacity gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership effects as an outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which projects produced partnership-related outcomes (93% reported partnership effects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document new partnerships formed, strengthened collaborations, and resultant resources or outputs attributable to partnerships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming effects as an outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which projects affected programming (91% reported programming effects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate new or changed programs, curriculum materials, exhibition content, or instructional approaches developed as part of the grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Museum profile and reputation effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes in museum profile (89% reported museum profile effects), such as greater visibility, recognition, or external requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture media coverage, requests for materials, invitations to collaborate, or changes in public/perceived reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance of audience effects to project type
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that audience effects vary by project focus — Programming, Exhibition, and Technology projects show higher audience effects, while Digitization/Collections and Organizational Development projects may be internally focused with audience effects less relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating outcomes, align expected outcomes with primary activity area and do not penalize internally focused projects for limited external audience effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data reporting and use of complete tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Use comprehensive data tables (Appendix D Table IV‑1 – IV‑30) to report frequencies and cross-tabulations for effects and characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present detailed tables for reproducibility and to support claims about effects by project area, museum size, and grant size.
